topics.title: Meaning and importance of business studies
topics.content:
Business studies is the subject that teaches us about the activities of buying, selling and producing goods and services, and how to keep money and records properly.

Why business studies is important:
- It prepares us for future jobs and careers, for example accountant, secretary, trader, banker.
- It teaches us how to start and manage our own business.
- It helps us keep simple records of money.
- It shows us honesty and good customer care.
- It helps us understand the offices and shops we see every day.

Goods are things we can see and touch that satisfy our needs, for example bread, shoes, books. Services are helpful acts people render for money, for example teaching, barbing, tailoring, laundry.

Evaluation questions:
1. Define business studies.
2. Mention four reasons why business studies is important.
3. Differentiate between goods and services with two examples each.

topics.title: The office: types and functions
topics.content:
An office is a room or building where clerical (paper) work of an organization is done. It is the centre where information is received, processed and sent out.

Types of office:
- Closed office: one or few workers have a private room. It gives privacy and quiet.
- Open office: many workers sit together in one big hall. It is cheaper and makes supervision easy.
- Small office: for a small business, for example a headmaster's office.
- Large office: for big organizations with many departments, for example a bank headquarters.

Functions of an office:
- Receiving and sending information (letters, calls, emails).
- Keeping records and files.
- Preparing documents like receipts and invoices.
- Making arrangements for meetings and visitors.
- Handling money matters of the organization.

Evaluation questions:
1. Define an office.
2. State the difference between a closed office and an open office.
3. Mention four functions of an office.

topics.title: Office staff and their duties
topics.content:
Different workers make an office run well. Each has his or her own duty.

- The manager: plans, directs and controls the whole organization.
- The accountant: keeps the money records of the organization.
- The secretary: types letters, keeps files, receives visitors and arranges meetings for the boss.
- The clerk: does daily records like filing, copying and simple accounts.
- The receptionist: welcomes visitors and answers telephone calls.
- The messenger or office assistant: carries documents and runs small errands.

Good office qualities: honesty, punctuality, neatness, politeness, hard work and the ability to keep secrets (confidentiality).

Evaluation questions:
1. Mention five office staff and one duty of each.
2. Who is a receptionist?
3. Why must an office worker keep secrets?

topics.title: Honesty in business
topics.content:
Honesty in business means being truthful and fair to customers, workers and the government.

How a business shows honesty:
- Selling goods at the correct price.
- Giving the correct change and issuing receipts.
- Selling goods that are of good quality, not fake or expired goods.
- Telling customers the truth about a product.
- Paying workers their wages on time.
- Paying tax to the government.

Advantages of honesty in business: customers keep coming back, the business grows, the business person enjoys peace and respect, and the government can trust the business.

Dishonest practices like cheating, lying about quality, hoarding goods to raise price and selling fake goods destroy a business name.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is honesty in business?
2. Mention four ways a business person can show honesty.
3. State three benefits of honesty in business.
